page: Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, running on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server includes a 472 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. The CPU architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES cryptography extensions, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core CPU stress tests and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range, with read-only large block memory bandwidth measured at 53.01 GB/s and write bandwidth at 34.32 GB/s. Database operations and Redis SET performance also align with average tier expectations, processing 12.85 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the system demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 340.4 tokens per second on small LLM models, though prompt processing on medium models is relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F4ads_v7 offers a balanced resource profile, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores with a substantial 472 GB local storage allocation. This eliminates the immediate need for external storage attachments for localized data tasks, optimizing resource density. The instance is well-suited for workloads requiring high single-thread performance alongside moderate memory capacity, such as web serving, relational database hosting, lightweight data processing, and small-scale language model inference.

It is highly suitable for web serving, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference.
